title: Minority attack, e-pawn break or a waiting move
outcomes: Chooses between the minority attack, the e-pawn break and a waiting move in positions where nobody names the plan
Checks whether the pieces are ready before the b-pawn is pushed, and sees that one displaced piece can change the answer
Recognises a position that only looks like the structure because White still has a c-pawn

steps.text: In **Carlsbad structure: the minority attack and its limits** you met the structure and its two plans. Now choose in a real position: the minority attack b4, the e-pawn break e4, or a waiting move that improves a piece. Rule of thumb: start b4 when the pieces are placed and nothing is left loose by the push; otherwise wait or play in the centre.

steps.caption: White to move. Carlsbad structure, but the pieces are not placed yet: the plan b4 would come too early.

line.say: A waiting move: it gives the bishop a retreat and starts no pawn plan yet.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** The minority attack needs a target (the c6 pawn after the exchange), time (the other side has no faster plan) and pieces placed so that b4 does not run into a counter. When one is missing, the e-pawn break or a waiting move is the plan. The next three positions differ by one feature; the question is always: is b4 reasonable?

steps.title: Same structure, the same pawn push
steps.prompt: Predict for each position whether b4 is a reasonable move. In the second and third, one Black bishop stands on another square.
Which of the three, target, time or placed pieces, was hardest for you to judge in this lesson? Write one thing you will check first next time.
